reviews.title: Disguised as a language-learning app, but in reality, it’s a cheap flirting platform for yellowfever
reviews.text:
非常差劲的平台，尤其是对女性用户的安全保障和举报处理态度。

HelloTalk 名义上是语言学习平台，但实际使用体验更像是一个低成本的跨国搭讪平台。其在小红书上的部分营销内容也频繁围绕“认识外国男生”“跨国交友”等话题吸引女性用户。平台享受着异性交友带来的流量，却不愿正视由此产生的安全风险。

我通过 HelloTalk 认识了一名男性用户，对方主动搭讪并索要我的微信，随后在微信上发送不雅裸照，并以建立亲密关系为由诱导我拍摄私密照片。

我向平台举报，提供了该用户的账号信息、联系方式及相关证据，微信也已认定相关行为违规。然而，HelloTalk 却反复以“行为发生在第三方平台”“缺乏站内直接证据”为由拒绝处理。

最令人愤怒的是，客服反过来教育我，说平台早已建议用户不要通过第三方软件交流。

请问，是我主动要求转移平台的吗？明明是对方通过 HelloTalk 主动索要我的微信，为什么平台不去核查他的站内行为，反而将责任推给举报者？

如果平台认为转移至第三方软件存在安全风险，为什么不首先审查主动引导用户转移平台的账号？为什么出了问题，反而要指责受到骚扰的人没有遵守安全建议？

更荒谬的是，平台以保护聊天隐私为由解释无法进一步核查，却又不断要求我提供更多站内证据。隐私保护当然重要，但这不应该成为敷衍举报、拒绝调查的万能借口。
更不应该用安全提示来反过来教育举报者。

一边利用跨国交友吸引用户，一边在网站内设立形同虚设禁止用户找亲密关系 色情。一边在用户遭遇骚扰后强调“不要去第三方平台”，这种前后矛盾的运营逻辑实在讽刺。

我对这个平台最失望的，不仅是遇到了不怀好意的用户，而是举报之后才发现，平台似乎更擅长解释自己为什么不需要负责，而不是认真解决用户反映的安全问题。

不推荐正常人使用。Extremely disappointing platform, especially when it comes to user safety and how harassment reports are handled.

HelloTalk claims to be a language-learning platform, but in reality, it often feels more like a low-effort international dating and flirting app. Some of its marketing content on Xiaohongshu even encourages women to join to meet foreign men. The platform benefits from attracting users through international dating and social connections who have fantasy for foreigners, yet refuses to take responsibility when those interactions lead to harassment.

My experience with HelloTalk has been absolutely disgraceful. I was a paying VIP member, yet my account was permanently banned for “political talks,” with no specific evidence provided to justify such an extreme punishment. I repeatedly asked HelloTalk to show me exactly which messages violated its policies, but all I received was a generic statement. They even claimed multiple users had reported me, yet failed to provide evidence demonstrating that I had engaged in political discussions with multiple people. How can a company permanently terminate a paying customer’s account without offering a clear, case-specific explanation?

Here is what actually happened: I did not initiate the political discussion. The other user made negative comments about my country, questioned my knowledge of Chinese history, and made an ignorant assumption that I knew nothing about their history. I responded by providing a summary of China’s history, and the user said it was difficult for them to comprehend. I never said anything bad about China. I was responding to a conversation someone else started, yet I was the one who received the permanent ban. If HelloTalk has rules restricting political discussions, those rules should be enforced fairly and consistently, rather than leaving users feeling that they have been punished simply for participating in a disagreement.

reviews.title: Extremely frustrating experience - DO NOT WASTE OF MONEY
reviews.text:
I downloaded HelloTalk because I genuinely wanted to use the app for its main purpose: practicing languages, meeting people from different backgrounds, and improving my speaking skills. Unfortunately, my experience has been extremely disappointing, especially when it comes to account management and customer support.

The biggest problem is that your account can apparently be banned without any meaningful explanation or a reasonable opportunity to resolve the issue.

In my case, I created a completely new account on a brand-new device and used the application for the first time. After only a few hours, my account was banned with a message saying that I had received multiple reports. This makes absolutely no sense from my perspective. It was a brand-new account, on a brand-new device, and I had barely had the opportunity to use the app. Being told that the account was banned because of “multiple reports” was extremely difficult to understand.

How can a brand-new account that has barely been used suddenly accumulate enough reports to justify a ban? If the system is automatically detecting and banning accounts based on reports, then there is clearly a serious problem with the way the moderation system works.

The Information Commissioner’s Office has said that:

* Refusing non-essential tracking should be as easy as accepting.

reviews.title: Can’t sign in
reviews.text:
The app says I can’t sign in because I supposedly violated their policy. I use the app to learn languages and practice with people I know who I met there. Occasionally, I join other rooms or host my own.

One day, I came across someone who appeared to be targeting underage girls, so I reported him. Later, there was a man and a woman discussing politics and saying some pretty extreme things. I reminded them that political discussions aren’t allowed on the app and suggested they follow the rules. Instead, they started insulting me and became even more political. I told them, “I’m sorry, but I’m going to report you,” reported the conversation, and left.

About 30 minutes later, I could no longer sign in to my account. After contacting HelloTalk several times, I was told that my device had been banned for talking about politics. I was extremely confused because I never participated in any political discussion. I even provided screenshots of the conversation, and the only things I said were that politics weren’t allowed on the app and that I would report the behavior if it continued.

It’s frustrating that people who appear to break the rules, including those engaging in inappropriate behavior, seem to remain on the platform, while users who are genuinely there to learn languages and help enforce the community guidelines can end up being banned. Based on my experience, the moderation and appeal process needs significant improvement.
